items.title: Validation rules
items.text:
• setting enforcement to evaluate for an organization on a non enterprise plan triggers an error
  • setting target must be one of branch, tag or push, any other value triggers an error
  • setting restricted_file_paths, max_file_path_length, restricted_file_extensions or max_file_size for a ruleset whose target is not push triggers an error
  • setting a rule that rulesets with target push do not support, e.g. copilot_code_review or commit_message_pattern, for a ruleset with target push triggers an error, a warning for the rules allows_*, requires_*, required_pull_request, required_status_checks and required_merge_queue
  • setting a rule required before merging a pull request, e.g. copilot_code_review or required_workflows, for a ruleset with target tag triggers an error
  • setting branch_name_pattern for a ruleset whose target is not branch, or tag_name_pattern for a ruleset whose target is not tag triggers an error
  • setting include_refs or exclude_refs for a ruleset with target push triggers a warning, as push rulesets apply to all refs of a repository
  • setting max_file_path_length outside the range [0, 32767], max_file_size outside the range [0, 100], or more than 200 entries or an entry longer than 200 characters in the lists of the push rules triggers an error
  • setting restricted_file_paths_exceptions while restricted_file_paths is empty, or max_file_size_exceptions while max_file_size is 0 triggers a warning
  • setting an invalid operator, an empty pattern, an invalid code scanning tool or threshold, an invalid code quality severity, a code coverage threshold outside the range [0, 100] or an invalid workflow triggers an error
  • setting a workflow whose path is not a .yml or .yaml file triggers a warning, e.g. because of an unescaped @ in the path
  • referencing the repository of a workflow by its id triggers an error, otterdog shows a repository by its id only if it can not resolve its name, e.g. if the repository was deleted
  • setting a push rule, required_code_quality or required_code_coverage for an organization on a free plan triggers a warning, as they require at least GitHub Team
  • setting a pattern, e.g. commit_message_pattern, or requires_license_compliance_scanning for an organization on a non enterprise plan triggers a warning, as they require GitHub Enterprise
  • setting required_code_quality, required_code_coverage or requires_license_compliance_scanning triggers an error, as they are only supported by repository rulesets
  • defining organization rulesets for an organization on a non enterprise plan triggers an error

items.title: Example usage
items.text:
The following ruleset would basically prevent force-pushes for the default branch of all repositories of the eclipse-csi GitHub organization:

jsonnet 
orgs.newOrg('eclipse-csi') {
  ...
  rulesets: [
    orgs.newOrgRuleset('main') {
      include_repo_names: [
        "~ALL"
      ],
      include_refs+: [
        "~DEFAULT_BRANCH"
      ],
      required_pull_request: null,
      required_status_checks: null,
    },
  ],
}

items.title: Secret Value
items.text:
A Secret Value is the value of a secret on organization, repository or environment level, or the secret of an organization or repository webhook.

As the configuration is stored in a repository, a secret value should not be written in clear text. Instead, it references the secret in a credential provider, using the format <credential_provider>:<provider specific data>. Otterdog resolves the reference when applying the configuration.

Provider Format Example Bitwarden bitwarden:<bitwarden item id>@<custom_field_key> bitwarden:118276ad-158c-4720-b68d-af8c00fe3481@secret Pass pass:<path/to/secret> pass:path/to/secret HashiCorp Vault vault:<path/to/secret>/<field> vault:path/to/secret/field

The setup of the credential providers is described in Credentials.

items.title: Redacted values
items.text: GitHub does not disclose secret values via its API. After executing an import operation, secret values are therefore set to ********. Resources with such a redacted value are skipped during processing: replace the value with a reference to a credential provider to manage the resource with otterdog.

items.title: Updating values
items.text: As otterdog does not maintain any local state and GitHub does not disclose secret values, otterdog can not detect that a value changed in the credential provider. Use the --update-secrets or --update-webhooks options of the apply operation to update them, limited to specific secrets or webhooks with --update-filter.

items.title: Validation rules
items.text:
• a value that does not reference a supported credential provider triggers a warning
  • a reference that the organization is not allowed to use, see Secret access policy, triggers an error, or a warning in warn mode
  • a redacted value (********) triggers a validation info, the resource will be skipped during processing

The following table captures all supported settings on organization level:

If true, property discussion_source_repository must be set as well has_organization_projects boolean If the organization can have organization projects has_repository_projects boolean If the repositories can have repository projects members_can_change_project_visibility boolean If members with admin permissions for a project can change its visibility members_can_change_repo_visibility boolean If members with admin permissions for a repo can change its visibility members_can_create_private_repositories boolean If members can create private repos members_can_create_public_pages boolean If members can create public GitHub Pages sites in this organization. If disabled, no GitHub Pages will not be published for the organization. members_can_create_private_pages boolean If members can create private GitHub Pages sites in this organization. If enabled on organization level, it overrides the setting on repo level custom_properties list[CustomProperty] Definition of custom properties workflows Workflow Settings Workflow settings on organizational level

The read-only property plan is not changed by apply. validate compares the settings and rules that require a paid plan, e.g. push rulesets, with the plan of the configuration, usually set by the default configuration: if plan is not set, validate does not warn about them.

items.title: Team Permissions
items.text:
The team_permissions property maps the slug of an organization team to the permission this team has on the repository:

team_permissions: {
  'committers': 'push',
  'project-leads': 'maintain',
},
Permission GitHub role Description pull Read Can read and clone the repository, open and comment on issues and pull requests triage Triage Can manage issues and pull requests without write access push Write Can read, clone and push to the repository maintain Maintain Can manage the repository without access to sensitive or destructive actions admin Admin Full access to the repository, including sensitive and destructive actions

Teams are referenced by their slug (e.g. a team named Project Leads has the slug project-leads), not by their display name. The team must exist in the organization, e.g. defined via orgs.newTeam.

Note

Team permissions are only managed when the default repository configuration of the template defines team_permissions, e.g. team_permissions: {}. Otherwise, otterdog does not retrieve the current team permissions from GitHub and any team_permissions set on a repository are ignored.

Warning

Once managed, team_permissions is authoritative: any team that has access to the repository on GitHub but is not listed will have its access removed. With team_permissions: {} as default value, this applies to every repository that does not explicitly declare its teams. Run otterdog plan to review such removals before applying. Permissions of individual collaborators are not affected, nor are permissions of teams excluded with exclude_teams unless the repository lists them, see Teams managed by another tool.

items.title: Jsonnet Function
Validation rules
items.text:
• specifying a description of more than 350 characters triggers an error (maximum supported length by GitHub)
  • specifying more than 20 topics triggers an error (maximum number of supported topics by GitHub)
  • disabling has_discussions while this repository is configured as source repository for discussion of this organization triggers an error
  • specifying a template_repository and forked_repository at the same time triggers an error
  • specifying a non-empty list of allow_action_patterns while allowed_actions is not set to selected, triggers a warning
  • specifying a permission in team_permissions other than pull, triage, push, maintain or admin triggers an error
  • specifying a code_security_configuration that is not defined in the code_security_configurations of the organization triggers an error
  • specifying a gh_pages_cname that is not a valid domain name or that is a github.io domain triggers an error
  • disabling secret_scanning while secret_scanning_push_protection is enabled triggers an error
  • specifying code_scanning_default_languages for a repository that does not exist yet, or with a language that is not detected in the repository, triggers an error

Tip

Changing the default branch of a repository has the same behavior as doing it via the Web UI. If the new branch already exists, the default branch will be switched, otherwise, the current default branch will be renamed to the newly specified name.

Note

When enabling GitHub Pages by setting gh_pages_build_type to either legacy or workflow, you should also define a github-pages environment, as it will be created automatically by GitHub.

Note

Setting gh_pages_cname only configures the custom domain on GitHub, the DNS records of the domain need to be configured separately, see configuring a custom domain. It is recommended to also verify the domain for the organization to prevent domain takeovers.

The HTTPS enforcement can only be changed once GitHub has issued a certificate for the custom domain, which can take some time after the domain has been configured. Until then, GitHub rejects any change to gh_pages_https_enforced, otterdog only logs a warning in that case and the change will be retried on the next apply.

When building GitHub Pages from a branch (legacy build type), GitHub stores the custom domain in a CNAME file at the root of the publishing source. If that file gets removed, e.g. by a workflow overwriting the branch, the custom domain will be removed as well.

Warning

Specifying a code scanning language that is not detected by GitHub in the repo itself will lead to an error during applying. In general, default setup for code scanning should be used with care as it has some weird behavior, using a custom workflow is the preferred way to use CodeQL. For the custom workflow to succeed, you need to disable the default setup though.

items.title: Example usage
Actor
items.text:
An Actor represents an entity that is allowed to perform certain actions. The following format is used to distinguish between the different types of actors that GitHub supports:

Actor Type Format Example User @<user-login> @netomi Team @<organization>/<team-slug> @OtterdogTest/committers App <app-slug> eclipse-eca-validation

items.title: Branch or Tag
items.text:
A BranchOrTag represents either a branch or tag pattern to use within an Environment. The following format is used to distinguish between tags and branches:

Type Format Example Branch <pattern> main Tag tag:<pattern> tag:v[0-9]*, tag:v[0-9].[0-9].[0-9]

For more information about the pattern matching syntax, see the Ruby File.fnmatch documentation.

items.title: Branch Protection Rule
items.text:
Definition of a Branch Protection Rule, the following properties are supported:

Key Value Description Notes pattern string Pattern to match branches that shall be protected by this branch protection rule Pattern follows fnmatch syntax, see doc@GitHub for more info requires_pull_request boolean If enabled, requires a pull request before merging. All commits must be made to a non-protected branch and submitted via a pull request before they can be merged into matching branches required_approving_review_count integer or null If specified, pull requests targeting a matching branch require a number of approvals and no changes requested before they can be merged. Only taken into account when requires_pull_request is enabled, should be set to null when requires_pull_request is disabled dismisses_stale_reviews boolean If enabled, dismiss approved reviews automatically when a new commit is pushed Only taken into account when requires_pull_request is enabled requires_code_owner_reviews boolean If enabled, require an approved review in pull requests including files with a designated code owner Only taken into account when requires_pull_request is enabled restricts_review_dismissals boolean If enabled, only allowed actors can dismiss reviews on pull requests Only taken into account when requires_pull_request is enabled review_dismissal_allowances list[Actor] List of actors that are permitted to dismiss reviews on pull requests Only taken into account when requires_pull_request is enabled bypass_pull_request_allowances list[Actor] List of actors able to bypass pull requests Only taken into account when requires_pull_request is enabled require_last_push_approval boolean Whether the most recent push must be approved by someone other than the person who pushed it Only taken into account when requires_pull_request is enabled requires_status_checks boolean If enabled, status checks must pass before branches can be merged into a matching branch requires_strict_status_checks boolean If enabled, pull requests targeting a matching branch must have been tested with the latest code. This setting will not take effect unless at least one status check is enabled required_status_checks list[StatusCheck] List of status checks that must succeed before branches can be merged Only taken into account when requires_status_checks is enabled requires_conversation_resolution boolean If enabled, all conversations on code must be resolved before a pull request can be merged into a matching branch requires_commit_signatures boolean If enabled, commits pushed to matching branches must have verified signatures requires_linear_history boolean If enabled, prevent merge commits from being pushed to matching branches requires_deployments boolean If enabled, environments must be successfully deployed to before branches can be merged into a matching branch required_deployment_environments list[string] List of environments that must be successfully deployed to before branches can be merged Only taken into account when requires_deployments is enabled lock_branch boolean If enabled, matching branches are read-only, users cannot push to the branch lock_allows_fetch_and_merge boolean Whether users can pull changes from upstream when the branch is locked. Set to true to allow fork syncing. Set to false to prevent fork syncing is_admin_enforced boolean If enabled, the above settings will apply to administrators and custom roles with the "bypass branch protections" permission as well restricts_pushes boolean If enabled, only allowed actors (see push_restrictions) will be able to push to matching branches. Required status checks will still prevent these actors from merging if the checks fail blocks_creations boolean If enabled, only allowed actors (see push_restrictions) will be able to create new branches matching this rule Only taken into account when restricts_pushes is enabled push_restrictions list[Actor] List of actors that are allowed to push to the matching branches Only taken into account when restricts_pushes is enabled allows_force_pushes boolean If enabled, actors with push permission can force push to matching branches This property takes precedence over bypass_force_push_allowances if enabled, allowing all users with write access to force push bypass_force_push_allowances list[Actor] List of actors able to force push to matching branches This property is only taken into account when allows_force_pushes is disabled allows_deletions boolean If enabled, allows actors with push permission to delete matching branches

Note

Property allows_force_pushes takes precedence of bypass_force_push_allowances. If it is enabled, any actor with write permissions can force push to matching branches. If you want to specify a list of actors that are allowed to force push, set allows_force_pushes to false and specify the allowed list of actors in bypass_force_push_allowances.

items.title: Jsonnet Function
items.text:
orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('<pattern>') {
  <key>: <value>
}

items.title: Validation rules
items.text:
• enabling a setting that is only taken into account when another setting is enabled, triggers a warning, e.g. dismisses_stale_reviews is only valid when requires_pull_request is enabled
  • specifying a non-empty list for a setting that is only taken into account when another setting is enabled, triggers a warning as well, e.g. bypass_pull_request_allowances is only valid when requires_pull_request is enabled
  • specifying an integer value for required_approving_review_count while requires_pull_request is disabled, triggers a warning, set it to null instead
  • specifying a non-empty list of bypass_force_push_allowances actors while allows_force_pushes is enabled, triggers a warning
  • specifying a non-empty list of review_dismissal_allowances actors while restricts_review_dismissals is disabled, triggers a warning
  • specifying a non-empty list of push_restrictions actors while restricts_pushes is disabled, triggers a warning

items.title: Example usage
Bypass Actor
items.text:
A Bypass Actor represents an entity that is allowed to bypass the restrictions setup by a specific ruleset. The following format is used to distinguish between the different types of actors that GitHub supports:

Actor Type Format Example Role #<role-name> #Maintain User @<github_handle> @alice Team @<organization>/<team-slug> @OtterdogTest/committers App <app-slug> eclipse-eca-validation

The following roles are currently supported:

  • Write
  • Maintain
  • RepositoryAdmin
  • OrganizationAdmin

Note

Deploy keys cannot be specified as bypass actors. Secret teams cannot be used as bypass actors, as GitHub only accepts visible teams, see Granting bypass permissions.

items.title: Bypass Mode
items.text:
If not specified, the bypass mode will be set to always by default, meaning that the specified bypass actor can bypass the restrictions of the ruleset in any case.

However, it is also possible to limit the ability to bypass the ruleset only for pull requests:

<actor>[:<bypass-mode>]?

Bypass Mode Description Format Example always Allow the actor to always bypass the restrictions <actor>:always #Maintain:always pull_request Allow the actor to only bypass the restrictions in the context of a pull request <actor>:pull_request @OtterdogTest/committers:pull_request

items.title: Repository Codespaces Secret
items.text:
Definition of a Codespaces Secret on repository level, the following properties are supported:

Key Value Description Note name string The name of the secret value SecretValue The secret value

Codespaces secrets are available as environment variables in the codespaces created for the repository, see Managing development environment secrets. They are managed independently of the Repository Secrets of GitHub Actions: a Codespaces secret and an Actions secret can have the same name and different values.

The value should reference a credential provider instead of being written in clear text, see SecretValue.

items.title: Jsonnet Function
items.text:
orgs.newRepoCodespacesSecret('<name>') {
  <key>: <value>
}

items.title: Validation rules
items.text:
• a name that is not uppercase triggers an error, as GitHub normalizes secret names to uppercase
  • redacted secret values (********) trigger a validation info and will skip the secret during processing

Repository Dependabot Secret
items.text:
Definition of a Dependabot Secret on repository level, the following properties are supported:

Key Value Description Note name string The name of the secret value SecretValue The secret value

Dependabot secrets are used by Dependabot, e.g. to access private registries, and are the only secrets available to workflows triggered by Dependabot, see Configuring access to private registries for Dependabot. They are managed independently of the Repository Secrets of GitHub Actions: a Dependabot secret and an Actions secret can have the same name and different values.

The value should reference a credential provider instead of being written in clear text, see SecretValue.

  <key>: <value>
}

items.text:

  • redacted secret values (********) trigger a validation info and will skip the secret during processing

items.title: Example usage
Ref Matcher
items.text:
The following formats are supported to match the refs to be included / excluded in rulesets, depending on the target of the ruleset:

Target Description Format Example branch, push match individual branch(es) refs/heads/<name> refs/heads/main or refs/heads/releases/**/* branch, push match the default branch ~DEFAULT_BRANCH ~DEFAULT_BRANCH branch, push match all branches ~ALL ~ALL tag match individual tag(s) refs/tags/<name> refs/tags/v1.0.0 or refs/tags/v* tag match all tags ~ALL ~ALL

Names and patterns follow the fnmatch syntax, in which * does not match /, see Using fnmatch syntax.

items.title: Validation rules
items.text: • specifying a pattern that does not match the formats supported for the target of the ruleset triggers an error

items.title: Repository Ruleset
items.text:
Definition of a Repository Ruleset, the following properties are supported:

Key Value Description Notes name string The name of this repository ruleset target string The target of this ruleset Possible values are branch, tag or push enforcement string The enforcement status of this ruleset Possible values are active, disabled or evaluate (evaluate only available when enterprise billing is enabled) bypass_actors list[BypassActor] List of actors able to bypass this ruleset include_refs list[RefMatcher] List of refs or patterns to include matching branches exclude_refs list[RefMatcher] List of refs or patterns to exclude matching branches allows_creations boolean If disabled, only allows users with bypass permission to create matching refs allows_deletions boolean If disabled, only allows users with bypass permission to delete matching refs allows_updates boolean If disabled, only allows users with bypass permission to push matching refs allows_force_pushes boolean If disabled, only allows users with bypass permission to force push matching refs required_status_checks StatusCheckSettings or null If specified, status checks must pass before branches can be merged into a matching branch requires_commit_signatures boolean If enabled, commits pushed to matching branches must have verified signatures requires_linear_history boolean If enabled, prevent merge commits from being pushed to matching branches requires_deployments boolean If enabled, environments must be successfully deployed to before branches can be merged into a matching branch required_deployment_environments list[string] List of environments that must be successfully deployed to before branches can be merged Only taken into account when requires_deployments is enabled required_pull_request PullRequestSettings or null If specified, requires a pull request before merging. All commits must be made to a non-protected branch and submitted via a pull request before they can be merged into matching branches required_merge_queue MergeQueueSettings or null If specified, merges must be performed via a merge queue copilot_code_review CopilotCodeReviewSettings or null If specified, request a review from Copilot automatically for new pull requests, if their author has access to Copilot code review Only supported by rulesets with target branch commit_message_pattern PatternSettings or null If specified, the message of the commits pushed to matching refs must match a pattern Not supported by rulesets with target push commit_author_email_pattern PatternSettings or null If specified, the email of the author of the commits pushed to matching refs must match a pattern Not supported by rulesets with target push committer_email_pattern PatternSettings or null If specified, the email of the committer of the commits pushed to matching refs must match a pattern Not supported by rulesets with target push branch_name_pattern PatternSettings or null If specified, the names of matching branches must match a pattern Only supported by rulesets with target branch tag_name_pattern PatternSettings or null If specified, the names of matching tags must match a pattern Only supported by rulesets with target tag restricted_file_paths list[string] List of file paths that can not be pushed, using fnmatch syntax, e.g. secrets/** Only supported by rulesets with target push, at most 200 entries of up to 200 characters restricted_file_paths_exceptions list[string] List of file paths that can be pushed even if they match restricted_file_paths Only taken into account when restricted_file_paths is not empty max_file_path_length integer The maximum number of characters of the paths of the files that can be pushed Only supported by rulesets with target push, allowed values in the range [0, 32767], 0 disables the rule restricted_file_extensions list[string] List of file extensions that can not be pushed, e.g. *.exe Only supported by rulesets with target push, at most 200 entries of up to 200 characters max_file_size integer The maximum size in megabytes of the files that can be pushed, files stored with Git LFS are not limited Only supported by rulesets with target push, allowed values in the range [0, 100], 0 disables the rule max_file_size_exceptions list[string] List of file paths that can exceed max_file_size Only taken into account when max_file_size is not 0 required_code_scanning CodeScanningSettings or null If specified, code scanning tools must provide results before branches can be merged into a matching branch Only supported by rulesets with target branch required_code_quality CodeQualitySettings or null If specified, the code quality results of a pull request must be resolved before it can be merged into a matching branch Only supported by rulesets with target branch required_code_coverage CodeCoverageSettings or null If specified, the line coverage of a pull request must meet thresholds before it can be merged into a matching branch Only supported by rulesets with target branch, in public preview on GitHub requires_license_compliance_scanning boolean If enabled, the dependencies added or changed by a pull request must comply with the license policy of the organization before it can be merged into a matching branch Only supported by rulesets with target branch

Rulesets support use-cases that can not be modelled with Branch Protection Rules, e.g. bypass actors that are exempted from all rules of a ruleset, while the bypass allowances of a Branch Protection Rule only lift the pull request requirement and required status checks still apply. See Rulesets or branch protection rules for a comparison and the features of rulesets that are not supported, and Protecting branches for examples, e.g. restricting the files that can be pushed with a ruleset with target push.

A ruleset with target push checks the content of every push, to any ref of the repository: GitHub only supports the push rules in it, restricted_file_paths, max_file_path_length, restricted_file_extensions and max_file_size. The rules protecting branches or blocking the merge of pull requests, e.g. requires_linear_history or required_code_scanning, have to be defined in a separate ruleset with target branch.

A rule missing from a ruleset, e.g. because the default template predates it, is not managed: plan reports no difference for it and apply keeps its current setting on GitHub, including its exceptions, e.g. restricted_file_paths_exceptions, while a rule set to its disabled value, e.g. null, is removed.

items.title: Validation rules
items.text:
• setting enforcement to evaluate for an organization on a non enterprise plan triggers an error
  • setting target must be one of branch, tag or push, any other value triggers an error
  • setting restricted_file_paths, max_file_path_length, restricted_file_extensions or max_file_size for a ruleset whose target is not push triggers an error
  • setting a rule that rulesets with target push do not support, e.g. copilot_code_review or commit_message_pattern, for a ruleset with target push triggers an error, a warning for the rules allows_*, requires_*, required_pull_request, required_status_checks and required_merge_queue
  • setting a rule required before merging a pull request, e.g. copilot_code_review or required_code_scanning, for a ruleset with target tag triggers an error
  • setting branch_name_pattern for a ruleset whose target is not branch, or tag_name_pattern for a ruleset whose target is not tag triggers an error
  • setting include_refs or exclude_refs for a ruleset with target push triggers a warning, as push rulesets apply to all refs of a repository
  • setting restricted_file_paths, max_file_path_length, restricted_file_extensions or max_file_size for a ruleset of a public repository triggers an error, as GitHub only supports push rules for private and internal repositories
  • setting max_file_path_length outside the range [0, 32767], max_file_size outside the range [0, 100], or more than 200 entries or an entry longer than 200 characters in the lists of the push rules triggers an error
  • setting restricted_file_paths_exceptions while restricted_file_paths is empty, or max_file_size_exceptions while max_file_size is 0 triggers a warning
  • setting an invalid operator, an empty pattern, an invalid code scanning tool or threshold, an invalid code quality severity or a code coverage threshold outside the range [0, 100] triggers an error
  • setting a push rule, required_code_quality or required_code_coverage for an organization on a free plan triggers a warning, as they require at least GitHub Team
  • setting a pattern, e.g. commit_message_pattern, or requires_license_compliance_scanning for an organization on a non enterprise plan triggers a warning, as they require GitHub Enterprise
  • setting required_workflows triggers an error, as it is only supported by organization rulesets, see Organization Ruleset

Key Value Description Note name string The name of the secret value SecretValue The secret value

The value should reference a credential provider instead of being written in clear text, see SecretValue.

items.title: Example usage
Status Check
items.text:
A Branch Protection Rule or Ruleset allows to reference certain status checks that are required to pass before a pull request can be merged into the target branch.

Source Format Example Workflow <job-name> Run CI App <app-slug>:<status-name> eclipse-eca-validation:eclipsefdn/eca Any any:<status-name> any:Run CI

Note

Rulesets do not make any distinction between Any or Workflow as source and thus specifying any: is not needed for them and will give the same result as omitting it.

items.title: Workflows as Required Status Checks
items.text:
Given the following workflows ci.yaml and job-legal.yaml in a GitHub repository:

ci.yamljob-legal.yaml 
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
    ...

jobs:
  build:
    ...

  test:
    name: testing
    ...

  call-legal:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/job-legal.yaml

name: legal
on:
  workflow_call:  # allow this workflow to be called from other workflows
    ...

jobs:
  legal:
    name: Legal Checks
    ...

Based on these workflow files, the following status checks would be available:

  • build: references the job build in the ci workflow by its id as it has no name specified
  • testing: references the job test in the ci workflow by its name testing
  • call-legal / Legal Checks: references the job legal by its name Legal Checks in the workflow job-legal.yaml that is called from the job legal in the ci workflow

Rules for translating jobs to stats-checks:

  • if a job has no name specified, use its id
  • if reusable workflows are called, join the jobs in their call hierarchy with /

Note

Be aware of the mandatory whitespaces surrounding the /. In case they are omitted, the status check will not be correctly recognized by GitHub. Please refer also the example outlined above.

Now, as an example to protect the main branch by enforcing specific status checks to pass before a pull request can be merged into it, you can add the status checks as below:

orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('main') {
    required_status_checks+: [
        "build",
        "call-legal / Legal Checks"
    ]
}

items.title: Identity provider integration
items.text:
The membership of a team can be managed by an identity provider (IdP), with one of these mechanisms:

  • team synchronization (team_sync): up to five IdP groups are connected to the team, available for organizations on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with team synchronization enabled
  • external groups (external_group_id): a single external group is connected to the team, available for organizations that are part of an enterprise using Enterprise Managed Users

Both mechanisms are mutually exclusive. The members of a team connected to an IdP are provisioned by the IdP, so members must not be set for such a team, and the current members of the team are ignored. When an existing team is connected to an external group for the first time, its current members are removed beforehand, as required by GitHub, once the external group has been found. They are restored with their role if the team can not be connected.

The connections to IdP groups are only retrieved from GitHub if the default configuration supports them, i.e. defines the newTeamSync function for team synchronization, or the external_group_id property in newTeam for external groups. If a mechanism is not available for an organization, it is skipped, while missing permissions of the credentials to retrieve them are reported as an error.

items.title: Jsonnet Function
items.text:
orgs.newTeam('<name>') {
  <key>: <value>
}

items.title: Validation rules
items.text:
• setting privacy must be one of visible or secret, any other value triggers an error
  • specifying a non-empty list of members while skip_members is enabled, triggers an error
  • specifying a user in members that is not yet an organization member while skip_non_organization_members is enabled, triggers an error
  • specifying both team_sync and external_group_id, triggers an error
  • specifying a non-empty list of members for a team connected to an identity provider group, triggers an error
  • specifying the same group id more than once in team_sync, triggers an error
  • specifying more than five groups in team_sync, triggers an error

items.title: Example usage
Team Sync
items.text:
Definition of an identity provider (IdP) group connected to a Team via team synchronization, the following properties are supported:

Key Value Description Note id string The id of the IdP group identifies the group name string The name of the IdP group required by the GitHub API description string The description of the IdP group

The available IdP groups of an organization, including their id, name and description, can be listed with the GitHub REST API.

Team synchronization requires an organization on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with team synchronization enabled, it is not available for organizations that are part of an enterprise using Enterprise Managed Users. Up to five IdP groups can be connected to a team.

Like other resources managed by otterdog, a group that is removed from team_sync is only disconnected from the team when applying the configuration with deletions enabled (--delete-resources). As long as a group stays connected, the members of the team are provisioned by the IdP and members is not applied.

items.title: Jsonnet Function
items.text:
orgs.newTeamSync('<id>') {
  <key>: <value>
}

items.title: Validation rules

items.title: Example usage
Policies
items.text:
Policies are a mechanism to enforce certain behavior within a project / organization. They can be defined on global or organization level. Any configured policy is also displayed in the dashboard.

If a policy is defined for an organization, its configured behavior can not be dismissed or ignored by the organization, unless the configuration is overwritten on organization level, i.e. on global level the use of macOS large runners is disabled, but it can be enabled per organization if it is eligible. In order to override the settings of policy, the same type must be used, as a consequence, there can only be one policy of a certain type be active for a single organization.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: Policies are defined using a yaml syntax and placed in the otterdog/policies folder of the config repository using either a .yml or .yaml extension.

items.title: Example
items.text:
name: a meaningful name of the policy
description: |-
  This is the description that will be displayed in the dashboard,
  and will also be included in any PR that will be opened if needed.
type: <policy-type>
config:
  ... # policy specific configuration

items.title: Settings
items.text: Setting Necessity Description name optional Name of the policy as displayed in the dashboard description optional Description of the policy as displayed in the dashboard type mandatory Type of the policy config mandatory Custom configuration dependent on the type of policy

items.title: Upload SBOM data to a dependency track instance
items.text: This policy will upload SBOM data as generated by workflows to a dependency track instance.
path: Upload SBOM data to dependency track

items.title: Configuration
items.text: • type - dependency_track_upload
path: Upload SBOM data to dependency track

items.title: Settings
items.text: Setting Necessity Value type Description artifact_name mandatory string The artifact to look for in workflow runs that contains SBOM data workflow_filter mandatory string Only consider workflows runs that reference the specified workflows
path: Upload SBOM data to dependency track

items.title: Example
items.text:
name: Upload sbom data to sbom.eclipse.org
description: |-
  This policy uploads generated sbom data to sbom.eclipse.org.
type: dependency_track_upload
config:
  artifact_name: "eclipse-sbom-data"
  workflow_filter: ".*/store-sbom-data.yml.*"
path: Upload SBOM data to dependency track

items.title: Restrict usage of macOS large runners
items.text:
To use a macOS large runner with GitHub Actions, one can just add something like that in a workflow file:

  runs-on: macos-latest-large

This will incur quite some costs as such runners are considerably more expensive than normal ones (see Billing for GitHub Actions).

This policy allows to control which organization / project is entitled to use such runners. If an organization is disallowed to use them, any workflow job that is queued on matching macOS large runners will be cancelled.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: • type - macos_large_runners

items.title: Settings
items.text: Setting Necessity Value type allowed mandatory boolean

items.title: Example
items.text:
name: Restrict use of macOS large runners
description: |-
  This policy restricts the use of macOS large runners for workflows using GitHub actions.
  If disallowed for an organization, any workflow job that uses such a runner is cancelled.
  In case your project wants / needs to use such runners, please open a ticket at the [HelpDesk](https://gitlab.eclipse.org/eclipsefdn/helpdesk/-/issues/new).
type: macos_large_runners
config:
  allowed: false

items.title: User Guide
items.text:
This guide is aimed at developers who use otterdog to manage GitHub organizations and repositories via an existing otterdog setup.

It focuses on the day-to-day workflow for making changes through configuration and pull requests, not on operating otterdog itself, see Operating Otterdog for that.

items.title: Making changes
items.text:
Every change to the configuration of an organization is a pull request on its configuration repository:

  • Workflow for changes: from the configuration repository to the changes applied on GitHub.
  • Adding resources: declare a new resource, e.g. a repository, with the function of the default configuration.
  • Renaming resources: rename a resource without deleting and recreating it.
  • Removing resources: delete a resource from the configuration.

items.title: Configuration Guides
items.text: The Configuration Guides start from common needs, e.g. protecting branches and tags, securing GitHub Actions or managing secrets, and explain how to address them with otterdog, including the trade-offs and limitations to consider. Start with the fundamentals: Inherited and explicit values and Reusing configuration with Jsonnet.

items.title: Troubleshooting & limits
items.text:
• Troubleshooting: understand a message of validate or an unexpected result of plan and apply.
  • Unsupported settings: the features and settings of GitHub that otterdog cannot manage.

items.title: Adding resources
items.text:
In order to add new resources to a given GitHub organization, the resources have to be declared at the correct location in the jsonnet configuration file (see supported Resources).

The resource has to be created with its corresponding jsonnet function as described in the respective section in the reference guide. By default, all parameter values as defined in the default configuration are inherited, but can be overwritten as needed.

items.title: Adding a new repository
items.text:
For example, we already have a GitHub organization testorg that already has a repository existing-repo:

orgs.newOrg('testorg') {
  ...
  _repositories+:: [
    ...
    orgs.newRepo('existing-repo') {
      description: "My first test repo",
      allow_auto_merge: true,
      ...
    },
}

Now we would like to add another repo with some specific settings that are different from the default config. Thus, we use the template function for creating a new repository newRepo and overwrite settings as needed.

orgs.newRepo('new-repo') {
  description: "My second test repo",
  allow_auto_merge: true,
  allow_merge_commit: false,
  allow_update_branch: false,
  dependabot_alerts_enabled: false,
  ...
}

Note

Otterdog comes with a builtin Playground to try out snippets and inspect the final manifestation of settings depending on the default configuration in use. It is available in the menu of the otterdog dashboard, and for each project with the default configuration of this project.

Finally, we need to add this snippet to the existing configuration, adding it to the _repositories key in the configuration file:

orgs.newOrg('testorg') {
  ...
  _repositories+:: [
    ...
    orgs.newRepo('existing-repo') {
      description: "My first test repo",
      allow_auto_merge: true,
      ...
    },
+   orgs.newRepo('new-repo') {
+     description: "My second test repo",
+     allow_auto_merge: true,
+     allow_merge_commit: false,
+     allow_update_branch: false,
+     dependabot_alerts_enabled: false,
+     ...
+   },
}

items.title: Removing resources
items.text: In order to remove existing resources from a given GitHub organization, the declared resources just have to be deleted from the jsonnet configuration file.

items.title: Removal of a webhook
items.text:
For example, we already have a GitHub organization testorg that has a webhook as defined like that:

orgs.newOrg('testorg') {
  ...
  webhooks+: [
    orgs.newOrgWebhook('https://ci.my.org/testorg/github-webhook/') {
      events+: [
        "create",
        "delete",
        "organization",
        "pull_request",
        "pull_request_review_comment",
        "push",
        "repository"
      ],
      ...
    },
  ],
}

In order to remove this webhook, simply delete its definition from the file:

orgs.newOrg('testorg') {
  ...
  webhooks+: [
-    orgs.newOrgWebhook('https://ci.my.org/testorg/github-webhook/') {
-      events+: [
-        "create",
-        "delete",
-        "organization",
-        "pull_request",
-        "pull_request_review_comment",
-        "push",
-        "repository"
-      ],
-      ...
-    },
  ],
}

items.title: Renaming resources
items.text:
In general, changing the unique identifier (e.g. the name of a repo, url of a webhook) of a resource in the configuration will result in the situation that the existing resource with the identifier will get deleted and a new resource with the new identifier gets created. See an example of the output of a plan operation where the url of a webhook has been changed:

- remove repo_webhook[url="https://www.example.org", repository="test-repo5"] {
-   active                                                   = true
-   content_type                                             = "form"
-   events                                                   = [
-     "push"
-   ],
-   insecure_ssl                                             = "0"
-   url                                                      = "https://www.example.org"
- }

+ add repo_webhook[url="https://www.example.org/webhook", repository="test-repo5"] {
+   active                                                   = true
+   content_type                                             = "form"
+   events                                                   = [
+     "push"
+   ],
+   insecure_ssl                                             = "0"
+   url                                                      = "https://www.example.org/webhook"
+ }

In some cases, re-creation of a resource is not an idempotent operation (especially in the case of a Repository) as some content of the resource would be lost in the process. Some resources support a list of aliases, which allows to specify previous identifiers of the same resource that will be used to associate current live resources with entries in the configuration.

After the changes have been applied, the aliases property can be safely remove as it is not needed anymore, but it can be left for traceability to know what the previous identifiers or a resource have been.

items.title: Supported resources
items.text:
• Organization Webhook
  • Repository
  • Repository Webhook

items.title: Example usage
items.text:
Taking the example from above, let's specify the previous identifier of the webhook in the aliases property:

Webhook 
webhooks: [
    orgs.newRepoWebhook('https://www.example.org/webhook') {
        aliases: ['https://www.example.org'],
        events+: [
            "push"
        ],
    },
],

The result of the plan operation for the Webhook would look like this now:

~ repo_webhook[url="https://www.example.org", repository="xxxxxxx"] {
~   url                 = "https://www.example.org" -> "https://www.example.org/webhook"
~ }

Analogously, the aliases property can also be specified for a repository, e.g. to rename an existing repository named oldreponame to newreponame:

Repository 
orgs.newOrg('testorg') {
  ...
  _repositories+:: [
    ...
    orgs.newRepo('newreponame') {
      aliases: ['oldreponame'],
      allow_auto_merge: true,
      allow_merge_commit: false,
      allow_update_branch: false,
      dependabot_alerts_enabled: false,
      web_commit_signoff_required: false,
      branch_protection_rules: [
        orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('main'),
      ],
    },
}

items.title: Unsupported settings
items.text:
Not all features or settings of a GitHub organization and its associated resources can be managed by the means of otterdog. The following non-exhaustive list outlines settings that are currently not supported:

  • setting the profile picture of an organization or a social media preview for a repository #119
  • manage release entries, packages, or deployments that should be visible on the main page
  • manage default repository labels on organization level
  • secrets and variables for Copilot agents
  • managing GitHub apps or oauth policies
  • managing pinned repositories for an organization
  • managing individual collaborators of repositories, use teams and team_permissions instead
  • supporting merge queue settings for a branch protection rule #86, use the required_merge_queue setting of a ruleset instead
  • ruleset rules and parameters other than those listed in Rulesets or branch protection rules, e.g. the required reviewers of the rule requiring a pull request
  • targeting the repositories of an organization ruleset by custom properties
  • deploy keys as bypass actors of a ruleset
  • requiring actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA in the GitHub Actions settings
  • transfer a repo from one organization to another organization
  • (deprecated) tag protections #143, use rulesets instead, see Protecting tags and releases

Most of the unsupported settings are only accessible via the Web UI of GitHub. In case you would like to have a specific feature of GitHub being supported by otterdog, please open a ticket.

items.title: Workflow for Changes
items.text: The typical workflow for making changes to your GitHub organization using otterdog is pull-request based and consists of the following phases:

items.title: 1. Prepare your change
items.text:
1. Find the configuration repository: Identify the otterdog configuration repository for your GitHub organization (e.g. .eclipsefdn, .repositories, or similar).

  2. Fork the repository (if needed): If you do not have write access, fork the repository according to your corporate guidelines or to your personal GitHub account. If you do not have write access and forking is not allowed, contact the organization maintainers.

  3. Clone the repository: Clone the configuration repository locally (e.g. gh repo clone <org>/.eclipsefdn).

  4. Create a feature branch: Create a branch from main for your change (e.g. git switch -c my-feature-branch).

  5. Edit configuration files: Make your changes in the configuration files. The main entry point is otterdog/<org>.jsonnet. See examples and tutorials and the Reference.

  6. Commit your changes: Commit with a clear and descriptive message.

items.title: 2. Open a Pull Request
items.text: 1. Push your branch and open a PR: Push your branch and open a Pull Request against the main branch of the configuration repository.

items.title: 3. Review and validation
items.text:
1. Automated checks run: Syntax validation and configuration diff analysis are executed automatically for the Pull Request.

  2. Request reviews: Request reviews as required for the type of change. Mandatory reviewers are assigned automatically.

  3. Address review feedback: Respond to review comments and update the Pull Request if necessary.

items.title: 4. Merge and apply
items.text: 1. Merge the Pull Request: Once approved, the Pull Request can be merged. This may be done by the reviewer or the author, see automated comments for details. The merge triggers otterdog to automatically apply the changes to the GitHub organization.

items.title: Configuration Guides
items.text: The guides in this section start from a need, e.g. protecting a release branch or limiting the permissions of workflows, and explain how to address it with otterdog: which properties to use, what the consequences of each choice are and which trade-offs to consider. They complement the Reference, which documents every supported property, and link to it instead of repeating it. To add, rename or remove a resource, see Making changes.

items.title: How to read the guides
items.text:
• Examples are complete and minimal: each example is a complete organization configuration that only contains the properties relevant to the topic. All other properties are inherited from the default configuration. The import statement at the top of the configuration file is omitted.
  • Examples use the example default configuration: the values that an example inherits come from the example default configuration. The default configuration of your organization may define different values, see Inherited and explicit values.
  • Examples can be tried out: the link below an example opens it in the Playground of the otterdog dashboard, which also lists all examples of these guides, and checks the values of the configuration like otterdog does. The link evaluates the example with the example default configuration. The Playground can also evaluate it with the default configuration of the otterdog instance, which may define other values, or not provide all of its functions.

  • Recommendations and policies are distinguished: guides mark general recommendations and choices that depend on the policy of your organization:

    Recommendation

    A practice that is recommended in general, usually based on the GitHub documentation.

    Organization policy

    A choice that depends on the requirements, the size or the governance of your organization.

  • GitHub plans matter: some GitHub features are only available for certain GitHub plans or repository visibilities. Otterdog cannot enable a feature that GitHub does not provide for your organization. Guides mention the relevant availability and link to the GitHub documentation, which remains the authoritative source.

items.text: Guide Read it when you want to ... Inherited and explicit values understand where a value comes from and why a plan shows a change Reusing configuration with Jsonnet share settings between many repositories without copying them

Protecting branches protect the default branch or release branches Organization-wide rulesets apply the same protection to many repositories Rulesets or branch protection rules choose between the two mechanisms Migrating to rulesets replace branch protection rules with rulesets without losing protection Protecting tags and releases prevent release tags from being moved or deleted

Securing GitHub Actions limit the permissions of workflows and control which actions can run Repository security features enable secret scanning, Dependabot, code scanning and vulnerability reporting, or apply code security configurations Secrets and variables provide credentials to workflows without exposing them Deployment environments protect deployments and publishing with approvals and branch restrictions Webhooks connect external services securely

Pull requests and merging choose the merge methods, enable auto-merge or a merge queue Repository features and metadata enable issues, discussions or a wiki, and describe repositories Common repository patterns configure websites, mirrors, templates, forks or archived repositories

items.text:
Guide Read it when you want to ... Troubleshooting understand a message of validate or an unexpected result of plan and apply Unsupported settings know which features and settings of GitHub otterdog cannot manage

Administrators who maintain the default configuration for several organizations will find related information in Organization-wide policies.

items.title: Protecting branches
items.text: Otterdog supports both mechanisms that GitHub offers to protect branches: repository rulesets and branch protection rules. This guide shows common protections with both mechanisms. To choose between them, see Rulesets or branch protection rules.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
Answer the following questions before writing a protection:

  • Which branches? Usually the default branch, sometimes also maintenance or release branches.
  • Which workflow? Direct pushes, pull requests with reviews, or pull requests without mandatory review.
  • Which checks? The exact names of the status checks that must pass, see Status Check.
  • Who may bypass the protection? Release automation, maintainers, administrators, or nobody.

items.title: Prevent force pushes and deletions
items.text:
The minimal protection keeps the history of a branch intact without imposing a pull request workflow: users with write access can still push directly, but they cannot rewrite the history or delete the branch.

RulesetBranch protection rule 
orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('default-branch') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          required_pull_request: null, // (1)!
          required_status_checks: null,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Without a pull request requirement and without status checks, the ruleset only blocks force pushes and deletions, which are blocked by default (allows_force_pushes and allows_deletions are false).

Open in the Playground

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      branch_protection_rules: [
        orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('main') {
          requires_pull_request: false,
          required_approving_review_count: null, // (1)!
          requires_status_checks: false,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Must be null when requires_pull_request is disabled, see the validation rules of Branch Protection Rule.

Open in the Playground

Recommendation

Protect at least the default branch of every active repository against force pushes and deletions. This protection does not change the way people work, but prevents the accidental loss of history.

items.title: Require pull requests and reviews
items.text:
Requiring a pull request ensures that every change is visible and checked before it reaches the branch. The following example requires one approval, dismisses approvals when new commits are pushed and requires that the most recent push is approved by someone else than its author.

RulesetBranch protection rule 
orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('default-branch') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          required_pull_request+: {
            required_approving_review_count: 1,
            dismisses_stale_reviews: true,
            requires_last_push_approval: true,
          },
          required_status_checks: null,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}

Open in the Playground

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      branch_protection_rules: [
        orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('main') {
          required_approving_review_count: 1,
          dismisses_stale_reviews: true,
          require_last_push_approval: true,
          requires_status_checks: false,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}

Open in the Playground

Organization policy

The number of required approvals is a trade-off between assurance and the capacity of the team:

  • 0 requires a pull request, so that checks run and changes are visible, but no review.
  • 1 requires a second person to look at every change.
  • 2 or more increases assurance, but can block small teams.

The example default configuration requires 2 approvals. Choose a value that the team can sustain, as a requirement that cannot be met tends to be bypassed.

Further options of the pull request requirement:

Need Ruleset (required_pull_request) Branch protection rule Request a review of the code owners requires_code_owner_review requires_code_owner_reviews Resolve all review conversations before merging requires_review_thread_resolution requires_conversation_resolution Restrict the merge methods of pull requests allowed_merge_methods not available

Code owner reviews require a CODEOWNERS file in the repository, see About code owners. The merge methods available for all branches of a repository are configured by the repository settings allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge and allow_rebase_merge.

items.title: Require status checks
items.text:
Required status checks ensure that continuous integration succeeded before a change is merged.

RulesetBranch protection rule 
orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('default-branch') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          required_pull_request+: {
            required_approving_review_count: 1,
          },
          required_status_checks+: {
            strict: true, // (1)!
            status_checks+: [
              "build",
              "test / unit-tests",
            ],
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Requires the branch of the pull request to be up to date with the target branch before merging.

Open in the Playground

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      branch_protection_rules: [
        orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('main') {
          required_approving_review_count: 1,
          requires_status_checks: true,
          requires_strict_status_checks: true, // (1)!
          required_status_checks+: [
            "build",
            "test / unit-tests",
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Requires the branch of the pull request to be up to date with the target branch before merging.

Open in the Playground

The names of the checks must exactly match the names reported to GitHub, see Status Check for the naming rules of workflow jobs.

Warning

A required check that never reports a status blocks the merge of every pull request. This happens for example when a workflow is skipped because of path or branch filters, see Handling skipped but required checks.

Recommendation

When a check is reported by a GitHub App, use the format <app-slug>:<check-name>, so that only this app can satisfy the check.

Requiring up-to-date branches (strict) guarantees that the checks ran against the latest state of the target branch, at the cost of more rebases and CI runs in busy repositories. A merge queue provides the same guarantee without requiring authors to update their branches. Otterdog supports merge queues for rulesets only, see required_merge_queue in Repository Ruleset.

items.title: Require code scanning results and Copilot reviews
items.text:
Rulesets can also block merges on the results of code scanning, and request a review from Copilot automatically for new pull requests.

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('default-branch') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          required_pull_request+: {
            required_approving_review_count: 1,
          },
          required_code_scanning: orgs.newCodeScanning() {
            code_scanning_tools+: [
              "CodeQL:high_or_higher:errors", // (1)!
            ],
          },
          copilot_code_review: orgs.newCopilotCodeReview() {
            review_on_push: true, // (2)!
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Blocks the merge if CodeQL reports security alerts of severity high or critical, or alerts of severity error.
  2. Copilot also reviews the new pushes to a pull request, not only its first version.

Open in the Playground

Code scanning has to be set up for the repository, see Repository security features. Copilot only reviews the pull requests of authors that have access to Copilot code review.

items.title: Require code quality, coverage and license compliance
items.text:
Repository rulesets can block merges on the code quality results, the line coverage and the license compliance of the dependencies of a pull request:

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  settings+: {
    plan: "enterprise", // (1)!
  },
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('default-branch') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          required_pull_request+: {
            required_approving_review_count: 1,
          },
          required_code_quality: orgs.newCodeQuality() {
            severity: "warnings", // (2)!
          },
          required_code_coverage: orgs.newCodeCoverage() {
            minimum_coverage: 80, // (3)!
            max_coverage_drop: 1,
          },
          requires_license_compliance_scanning: true, // (4)!
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Read-only property that reflects the billing plan of the organization. The code quality and code coverage rules require at least GitHub Team, the license compliance rule GitHub Enterprise, validate warns otherwise.
  2. Code quality results of severity warning or error must be resolved before a pull request can be merged.
  3. A pull request is blocked if its line coverage is below 80 %, or drops by more than 1 percentage point compared to the default branch. GitHub does not wait for coverage uploads: make the checks that upload coverage data required status checks. This rule is in public preview on GitHub.
  4. The dependencies added or changed by a pull request must comply with the license policy of the organization.

Open in the Playground

These rules are only supported by repository rulesets, not by organization rulesets.

items.title: Restrict commit messages and branch names
items.text:
Patterns can enforce conventions for the metadata of commits, e.g. their message or the email of their author, and for the names of branches:

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  settings+: {
    plan: "enterprise", // (1)!
  },
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('commit-messages') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          required_pull_request: null,
          required_status_checks: null,
          commit_message_pattern: orgs.newPattern() {
            name: "Conventional Commits",
            operator: "regex", // (2)!
            pattern: "^(feat|fix|docs|chore|refactor|test|ci|build|perf|revert)(\\(.+\\))?!?: ",
          },
        },
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('branch-names') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~ALL",
          ],
          exclude_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          allows_creations: true, // (3)!
          allows_deletions: true,
          allows_force_pushes: true,
          required_pull_request: null,
          required_status_checks: null,
          branch_name_pattern: orgs.newPattern() {
            name: "Branch prefix",
            operator: "regex",
            pattern: "^(feature|fix|release|dependabot)/", // (4)!
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Read-only property that reflects the billing plan of the organization. Restricting the metadata of commits and the names of branches requires GitHub Enterprise, validate warns otherwise.
  2. The operator is one of starts_with, ends_with, contains or regex, set negate: true to reject the values that match the pattern instead, see Pattern Settings.
  3. The ruleset only restricts the names of branches: creating, deleting and force pushing branches stay allowed.
  4. Branches created by automation, e.g. Dependabot, must match the pattern too.

Open in the Playground

commit_author_email_pattern and committer_email_pattern restrict the emails of the commits in the same way. A branch name pattern is only supported by rulesets with target: "branch".

items.title: Restrict the files that can be pushed
items.text:
A ruleset with target push blocks pushes that add files matching restricted paths or extensions, files whose path is too long or files that are too large, to any branch of the repository. Push rulesets are only available for private and internal repositories.

A push ruleset checks the content of every push, to any ref of the repository and of its fork network: it has no target branch and no pull request to block. GitHub therefore only supports the push rules in a push ruleset, the rules protecting branches, e.g. requires_linear_history, and the rules blocking the merge of pull requests, e.g. required_code_scanning or required_code_quality, have to be defined in a separate ruleset with target branch:

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  settings+: {
    plan: "team", // (1)!
  },
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      private: true, // (2)!
      allow_forking: false,
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('default-branch') { // (3)!
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          requires_linear_history: true,
          required_code_quality: orgs.newCodeQuality() {
            severity: "warnings",
          },
        },
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('restrict-files') {
          target: "push",
          allows_creations: true, // (4)!
          allows_deletions: true,
          allows_force_pushes: true,
          required_pull_request: null,
          required_status_checks: null,
          restricted_file_paths+: [ // (5)!
            ".env",
            "secrets/**",
          ],
          restricted_file_paths_exceptions+: [ // (6)!
            "secrets/README.md",
          ],
          max_file_path_length: 255, // (7)!
          restricted_file_extensions+: [
            "*.exe",
            "*.jar",
          ],
          max_file_size: 10, // (8)!
          max_file_size_exceptions+: [ // (9)!
            "docs/assets/**",
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Read-only property that reflects the billing plan of the organization. Push rulesets require at least GitHub Team, validate warns otherwise.
  2. Push rulesets require a private or internal repository. The default settings of an organization disable the forking of private repositories.
  3. The rules protecting the default branch and blocking the merge of pull requests into it are defined in a ruleset with target branch, the default target of orgs.newRepoRuleset.
  4. A push ruleset only supports push rules, the branch rules enabled by orgs.newRepoRuleset have to be disabled.
  5. The paths of the files that can not be pushed, using fnmatch syntax.
  6. The paths of the files that can be pushed even if they match restricted_file_paths.
  7. The maximum number of characters of the path of a file, between 1 and 32767.
  8. The maximum size of a file in megabytes, between 1 and 100, files stored with Git LFS are not limited.
  9. The paths of the files that can exceed max_file_size.

Open in the Playground

validate reports the rules that a push ruleset does not support: an error for the rules blocking the merge of pull requests and the patterns restricting commit metadata or names of refs, and a warning for the branch rules that orgs.newRepoRuleset enables by default, e.g. allows_force_pushes or required_pull_request, to keep the configurations defining push rulesets before otterdog supported push rules valid.

items.title: Protect maintenance and release branches
items.text:
Maintenance branches often need the same protection as the default branch. A ruleset can protect several branch patterns at once, while a branch protection rule matches a single pattern.

RulesetBranch protection rule 
orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('protected-branches') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
            "refs/heads/release/*",
          ],
          allows_creations: true, // (1)!
          required_pull_request+: {
            required_approving_review_count: 1,
          },
          required_status_checks: null,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. By default, only bypass actors can create branches that match a ruleset. Allow creations if contributors should be able to create new release branches.

Open in the Playground

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      branch_protection_rules: [
        orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('main') {
          required_approving_review_count: 1,
          requires_status_checks: false,
        },
        orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('release/*') {
          required_approving_review_count: 1,
          requires_status_checks: false,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}

Open in the Playground

Patterns follow the fnmatch syntax with the File::FNM_PATHNAME flag: * does not match /. Use release/**/* to match nested names like release/1.x/fixes, see About branch protection rules.

Note

Only one branch protection rule applies to a branch: a rule that names the branch exactly takes precedence over patterns, and among patterns the rule created first wins. All matching rulesets apply together, and the most restrictive version of each rule is enforced. Restricting the creation of matching branches is done with allows_creations for rulesets, and with restricts_pushes and blocks_creations for branch protection rules.

items.title: Allow automation to push
items.text:
Release automation sometimes needs to push to a protected branch, e.g. to commit a version change. Grant such an exception to the narrowest possible actor.

RulesetBranch protection rule 
orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('default-branch') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~DEFAULT_BRANCH",
          ],
          bypass_actors+: [
            "my-release-app", // (1)!
            "@my-org/release-managers:pull_request", // (2)!
          ],
          required_pull_request+: {
            required_approving_review_count: 1,
          },
          required_status_checks: null,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. A GitHub App, referenced by its slug, can always bypass the ruleset.
  2. Members of this team can only bypass the ruleset when merging a pull request, not by pushing directly.

Open in the Playground

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-repo') {
      branch_protection_rules: [
        orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('main') {
          required_approving_review_count: 1,
          requires_status_checks: false,
          bypass_pull_request_allowances+: [
            "my-release-app",
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}

Open in the Playground

See Bypass Actor and Actor for the supported formats. The two mechanisms differ:

  • a ruleset bypass actor bypasses all rules of the ruleset, either always or only when merging a pull request
  • a branch protection rule bypass allowance only lifts the pull request requirement, required status checks still apply

Recommendation

Prefer a GitHub App or a dedicated team over individual user accounts as bypass actors: their permissions can be reviewed and revoked without changing the protection, and they do not depend on a single person.

Warning

Avoid repository roles such as #Write as bypass actors of a ruleset that requires pull requests: every user with this role could then merge without review, which makes the requirement optional.

items.title: Read-only branches and mirrors
items.text:
Some branches must not receive changes at all, e.g. a branch that is mirrored from another system or a frozen maintenance branch.

RulesetBranch protection rule 
orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-mirror') {
      rulesets: [
        orgs.newRepoRuleset('read-only') {
          include_refs+: [
            "~ALL",
          ],
          allows_updates: false,
          bypass_actors+: [
            "my-mirror-app", // (1)!
          ],
          required_pull_request: null,
          required_status_checks: null,
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Only the app that synchronizes the mirror can push.

Open in the Playground

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-mirror') {
      branch_protection_rules: [
        orgs.newBranchProtectionRule('main') {
          requires_pull_request: false,
          required_approving_review_count: null,
          requires_status_checks: false,
          restricts_pushes: true,
          push_restrictions+: [
            "my-mirror-app", // (1)!
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  ],
}
  1. Only the app that synchronizes the mirror can push.

Open in the Playground

A branch protection rule can also lock a branch completely with lock_branch, see Branch Protection Rule. Restricting who can push to a branch is only available for repositories owned by an organization, see About protected branches.

items.title: Administrators
items.text:
The two mechanisms treat administrators differently:

  • a branch protection rule does not apply to repository administrators and roles with the "bypass branch protections" permission, unless is_admin_enforced is enabled
  • a ruleset applies to everybody, except the actors listed in bypass_actors, e.g. #RepositoryAdmin or #OrganizationAdmin

Organization policy

Exempting administrators allows fixing a broken branch quickly, while enforcing the protection for them guarantees that every change follows the same process. If administrators need an exemption, make it explicit as a bypass actor of a ruleset, which is visible to everybody with read access to the repository.

items.title: Common pitfalls
items.text:
• Default branch renamed: a branch protection rule matches a branch name or pattern and must be updated when the default branch is renamed, while ~DEFAULT_BRANCH in a ruleset always follows the default branch.
  • Ignored settings: when requires_pull_request or requires_status_checks is disabled in a branch protection rule, the related settings are ignored, and validate reports them.
  • Archived repositories: GitHub does not allow changes to archived repositories, otterdog ignores their branch protection rules.
  • Protections defined outside otterdog: as otterdog manages all branch protection rules and rulesets of a repository, protections created in the GitHub web interface are removed when the configuration is applied with deletions enabled, see Rulesets or branch protection rules.

items.title: Deployment environments
items.text:
A GitHub Actions job that references an environment can only run once the protection rules of the environment are satisfied, and only then gets access to the secrets of the environment. Environments are therefore the right place for credentials that deploy or publish something.

Property Effect deployment_branch_policy, branch_policies all: no restriction, protected: only protected branches, selected: only the branches and tags listed in branch_policies reviewers, prevent_self_review users or teams who must approve the job, optionally not the person who triggered it wait_timer minutes to wait before the job can run secrets, variables values only available to jobs that use the environment

Users with GitHub Free can only configure environments for public repositories, and some protection rules have limited availability for private repositories, see Managing environments for deployment.

items.title: Protect publishing credentials
items.text:
The following environment is only available to workflows running for a tag starting with v, and requires the approval of a release manager other than the person who triggered the workflow:

orgs.newOrg('my-project', 'my-org') {
  _repositories+:: [
    orgs.newRepo('my-library') {
      environments+: [
        orgs.newEnvironment('release') {
          deployment_branch_policy: "selected",
          branch_policies+: [
            "tag:v*", // (1)!
          ],
